rulings.section: §7.4 item 1; §11 row 'What component the factory fitted at the top of the POWER strip'; §12 bullet 'The dark round component at the top of the POWER strip is the power indicator lamp'
rulings.currentText: "1. **A dark round component - identity not settled and it varies between units.** ... No manual mentions a fuse anywhere and MM's spare-parts list (6431-6491) contains no fuse, which argues the fuseholder is a later owner repair - **not proven either way.** [verified as two observations / unverified as to the stock part]"  and the §11 row whose 'what would settle it' column reads "MM p.3 carries a Power Supply circuit diagram **as an image the text layer does not include** - render that page and read it."
rulings.ruling: CLOSE THIS OPEN ITEM. The page was rendered and read. Replace the §7.4 item-1 body with: 'A dark round component. **The factory part here is the red power light**; the black FUSE holder on PH2 is a later owner modification. MM p.3's Power Supply Circuit Diagram enumerates the whole power-panel circuit - POWER CORD, POWER SWITCH, BLACK WIRE, TRANSFORMER, YELLOW/BLACK WIRE, RECTIFIER, CIRCUIT BREAKER, POWER LIGHT and the + / - outputs - and contains no fuse. MM p.4 step 8 treats the power light as a replaceable panel item ("Remove the burned-out power light and replace it with a new light assembly"), and the spare-parts list carries 6435 Light Assembly at $1.00 and no fuse anywhere in 6431-6491. On PH2 the fuseholder cap is oversize and physically overhangs the top line of the CIRCUIT BREAKER legend, hiding "CIRCUIT" - a factory fit would not obscure its neighbour\'s legend; on PH3 a red domed jewel on a knurled threaded barrel sits in the same position with CIRCUIT BREAKER fully legible. [verified] that the factory power panel carried a power light and no fuse - MM pp.3, 4, 11; [likely] that this position is where it is mounted - PH3, B1 p.3.'  In §11, replace the whole row with a much narrower residual: 'Whether the stock pilot lamp\'s lens/bezel matches the twelve panel lamps or is a separate jewel type. Fallback: draw the red jewel on a knurled barrel as seen on PH3.'  In §12, change the struck bullet\'s correction from 'Identity not settled and it varies between units' to 'Identity settled: stock = red power light, PH2\'s fuseholder is a non-factory addition.'
rulings.evidence: raw/pdf/maintenance-manual.pdf rendered at 300 dpi, PDF p.5 = printed p.3 (PDF p.4 carries the printed footer '2', so MM printed page = PDF page - 2): the 'Power Supply Circuit Diagram' is read directly off the image; every component is labelled and there is no fuse symbol. MM printed p.4 step 8 and the printed p.11 spare-parts list read from the OCR text, which matches the images. PH2 crop native x=3760 y=620 w=460 h=420 at 3x (fuseholder overhanging 'CIRCUIT'); PH2 crop x=3900 y=645 w=110 h=110 at 8x (cap face). PH3 crop x=3200 y=1500 w=240 h=260 at 4x (red jewel, CIRCUIT BREAKER legible).

rulings.currentText: "On PH2 it is a black knurled bayonet **fuseholder cap**, engraved `FUSE` three times radially around a curved rotation arrow."
rulings.ruling: Change 'three times radially around a curved rotation arrow' to 'four times radially around two curved rotation arrows'. Read at 8x the cap face carries FUSE at roughly 12, 3, 6 and 9 o'clock (the 6 o'clock instance inverted) with two short curved arrows inside the ring of text.

rulings.section: §5 bullet 'Every jack hole is encircled by a thin light ring'; §11 row 'Whether the light ring around each jack hole is printed ink or exposed substrate'
rulings.currentText: "**Every jack hole is encircled by a thin light ring**, on the dark field and on the blue stripes alike. Whether it is printed ink or the drilled edge exposing a light substrate is not settled. A redraw that omits it looks wrong. [verified as appearance / unverified as cause] - PH2"  and the matching §11 row.
rulings.ruling: SETTLE IT: the ring is **printed ink**. In the MATRIX the ring is demonstrably part of the printed artwork - each M10/M11 hole's cream ring is continuous with the cream bar that joins it to its neighbour, one stroke of the same weight and colour, and the drilled hole sits visibly off-centre inside its own ring (drilling tolerance against printed artwork). The rings on ordinary section jacks are the same colour and stroke weight. Retag: '[verified] printed, in the MATRIX; [likely] as a whole-panel rule - PH2'. Delete the §11 row, or reduce it to the residual '[likely] that the section jacks' rings are the same printed element as the matrix's, rather than a coincidentally similar drilled halo'.
rulings.evidence: PH2 crop native x=3050 y=780 w=210 h=200 upscaled 5x, and x=3060 y=790 w=130 h=130 upscaled 7x: the M10 loop's top bar, bottom bar and both verticals terminate in - and are continuous with - the hole rings. Compare PH2 crop x=745 y=1590 w=110 h=40 at 11x (an ordinary R-terminal pair): same cream, same ~3-4 px stroke, same per-hole eccentricity.

rulings.section: §7.5 last bullet; §11 row 'Whether the two pale marks at the upper left of the DECIMAL block are fasteners or finish damage'
rulings.currentText: "Two small pale marks on the dark field at the upper left of the block, above the `16 ARM` terminal. At 4208 px these read less like rivet heads and more like **chips in the dark finish exposing a light-coloured substrate underneath** - weak evidence bearing on the unresolved panel-material question, not a fastener claim. [unverified] - PH2"
rulings.ruling: SETTLE IT: they are finish damage, not fasteners. At 4x the two marks are irregular and ragged-edged, flat, matte and chalky-white, flush with the panel and casting no shadow - unlike the slide-switch discs, which are perfectly circular, slightly domed and cast a shadow to the lower right under the same lighting. Retag the bullet '[verified] that they are not fasteners; [likely] that they are chips exposing a lighter substrate or primer - PH2'. Delete the §11 'fasteners or finish damage' row. Then strengthen the §9/§11 substrate entries: the dark field is a **coating over a distinctly lighter, chalky off-white core** - the field is not a self-coloured dark material - which narrows the candidate list even though no source names the material.
rulings.evidence: PH2 crop native x=3100 y=1290 w=400 h=240 upscaled 4x (the two marks at approx. native (3230,1395) and (3190,1425)); compare PH2 crop x=760 y=1725 w=200 h=70 upscaled 8x (the slide-switch disc, round, domed, with a lower-right shadow).

rulings.section: §6 Band 5, bullet beginning 'Flanking each slide switch'
rulings.currentText: "Flanking each slide switch, one under the R/U column and one under the T/W column: **two round pale discs**, most likely the switch's panel-mounting rivet heads. ... [likely] - MM p.9; PH2. No source states that the visible discs *are* those rivet heads."
rulings.ruling: Correct the position and strengthen the evidence, keep the tag at [likely]. The discs are NOT under the R/U and T/W columns - they sit inboard of them, about three-quarters of a column pitch either side of the switch centre. Measured on PH2 section 2: left disc centre native x=805 against an R/U column centre of 774; right disc x=994 against a T/W column centre of 1029; column pitch 127 px, disc separation 189 px. Add two supports the file does not have: (a) at 8x the discs are slightly domed and cast a shadow to the lower right, so they are physical fasteners, not printing; (b) MM p.5 says the POWER switch is likewise rivet-mounted - 'To replace the power switch, remove the leads from the terminals and drill out the rivets which hold the switch. Insert a new power switch, fastening it with machine screws and nuts' - which is a second, independent switch that MM calls rivet-held and that shows the same two pale discs (above ON and below OFF) on the panel face.
rulings.evidence: PH2 crop native x=690 y=1540 w=480 h=250 at 3x (positions measured against the R/S/T and U/V/W hole centres in the same crop); PH2 crop x=760 y=1725 w=200 h=70 at 8x (relief and shadow). MM printed p.5 = PDF p.7.

rulings.section: Implementer summary item 1; §1 bullets 2, 3 and 4; §7.4 item 3; §12 bullet 'The panel is divided by a full-height printed vertical stripe'
rulings.currentText: "...MM pp.2, 4" (Implementer summary 1 and the §12 bullet); "'Push the power panel out of the computer console through the holes in the dividing section.' [verified] - MM p.4"; "...reached 'through the three-inch hole in the bottom of the computer.' [verified] - MM pp.2, 4"; "The bottom panel comes off 'by unscrewing the screws from the rubber feet.' [verified] - MM p.3"; "[verified] - B1 p.3; MM pp.4-5" (circuit breaker).
rulings.ruling: Every MM page number in §1 is one or two too high. MM printed page = PDF page - 2 (PDF p.4 carries the printed footer '2'). Correct to: 'unscrewing the screws from the rubber feet' -> **MM p.1** (Routine Maintenance / Oiling, PDF p.3); 'store the power cord in the compartment under the power panel ... through the three-inch hole in the bottom' -> **MM p.1** (Storage, PDF p.3); 'Push the power panel out of the computer console through the holes in the dividing section' -> **MM p.3** (Power Supply step 5, PDF p.5). So 'MM pp.2, 4' becomes **'MM pp.1, 3'** in both the Implementer summary and §12, and 'MM p.4' becomes 'MM p.3'. For the circuit breaker, 'MM pp.4-5' becomes **'MM pp.3-4'** (reset instruction is step 2 on printed p.3; the check-and-replace procedure is step 9 on printed p.4; printed p.5 is the power switch, transformer and rectifier and says nothing about the breaker). The §9 'Ratings behind the panel - MM pp.2-3' citation is CORRECT and must not be touched.
rulings.evidence: pdftotext page by page over raw/pdf/maintenance-manual.pdf: PDF p.4 ends '...remove all pro' + footer '2'; PDF p.5 ends with the Power Supply Circuit Diagram caption + footer '3'; PDF p.6 ends '...a new circuit breaker and replace the leads.' + footer '4'. PDF p.3 therefore carries printed p.1 (Cleaning / Storage / Relay Contacts / Oiling) and holds both the rubber-feet and three-inch-hole sentences.

rulings.currentText: "Letter designators (`A B C E F G H J K L N R S T U V W X Y Z`) print **below** their hole pair, centred on it to within a pixel at PH2 resolution."
rulings.ruling: 'Centred to within a pixel' is measurably wrong and should be replaced with the measured bias. Every silkscreen label on the panel - terminal letters, group legends and the section numerals alike - is set a consistent **4-7 px left of the centre of the thing it labels** at PH2's 4208 px width, roughly a fifth of a letter width. Measured, section 2 BINARY OUTPUT: A-pair holes at x=747.1 / 790.9 (centre 769.0), the letter A's brightness centroid at 763.3; B-pair 1002.5 / 1047.1 (centre 1024.8), letter B at 1017.8. The sign does NOT flip on the right-hand half of the panel (section 6: letter H 3 px left of its pair centre, letter J 7 px left; ARM 2-3 px left; N.C. 4 px left), so it is artwork, not perspective. Same bias on the group legends: COMMON's centre is 810 against its four holes' centre of 817; CAPACITOR 1022 against 1028; the section numeral 6 at 880 against its lamp's panel-level bezel centre of 898. Replace the clause with: 'set very slightly left of centre - a consistent 4-7 px at PH2 resolution, about a fifth of a letter width. Centring them in a redraw is acceptable; claiming they are centred is not.' The substantive rule (letters below, `+`/`-` above, decimal numerals to the left) is unaffected and stays [verified].
rulings.evidence: Numeric measurement on PH2: hole centroids by dark-blob column analysis and letter centroids by brightness-weighted centroid over the letter band, on the BMP conversion of PH2 crops at native x=690 y=320 w=460 h=130 (section 2) and x=2520 y=1150 w=470 h=130 (section 6); PH2 crop x=690 y=1345 w=500 h=120 at 4x for COMMON / CAPACITOR; x=2350 y=250 w=560 h=200 at 3x for the numeral 6.

rulings.currentText: The ASCII draws the matrix inside a closed grid - `+--------+--------+--------+` above the top row, between every row, and below the bottom row, with `|` down both outer sides of every cell.
rulings.ruling:
Redraw it as a bare tic-tac-toe hash. There is **no outer border rule and no rule below the bottom row or above the top row**; only two long verticals and two shorter horizontals, crossing. On PH2 the two verticals are the longer pair (they run from above the top row of holes to below the bottom row) and the two horizontals are the shorter pair (they stop short of the outer cells' holes at both ends). The section's own prose already says this correctly ('two long vertical and two long horizontal cream rules drawn between the cells, not touching any hole') - it is the diagram that contradicts the prose and the photograph, and a renderer following the diagram will draw a boxed grid. Suggested replacement form:

```
            |        |
     o-o    |  o-o   |  o-o        o-o
       1    |    2   |    3        | |
     o-o    |  o-o   |  o-o        o o
  ----------+--------+----------   | |
     o-o    |  o-o   |  o-o        o-o
       8    |    9   |    4         11
     o-o    |  o-o   |  o-o
  ----------+--------+----------
     o-o    |  o-o   |  o-o
       7    |    6   |    5
     o-o    |  o-o   |  o-o
            |        |
```
(with M10 drawn to the left of the board on the middle row's height, as now).
rulings.evidence: PH2 crop native x=3000 y=540 w=1120 h=700 at 2x: the two vertical rules overrun the top and bottom rows of cells; the two horizontal rules are inset at both ends; no rule runs round the outside of the 3x3 board.

rulings.currentText: "All block and group legends: heavy, wide, sans-serif grotesque, all caps. Generous letterspacing on the long band titles ...; tighter on `STORAGE/PROCESSING` and the small labels."
rulings.ruling: Add one clause a redraw needs: the small group legends are letterspaced too, so `N.O.` and `N.C.` read on the panel as **`N. O.`** and **`N. C.`** - a clear gap follows each period. It is tracking, not a typed space; a redraw should track the group legends out rather than set them tight, or the labels will not match the photograph. Also drop the claim that `STORAGE/PROCESSING` is tracked tighter than the band titles - at 8x its letterspacing is comparable to `BINARY OUTPUT`; the file gives no measurement behind 'tighter' and should not assert it.
rulings.evidence: PH2 crop native x=1170 y=1120 w=420 h=70 upscaled 8x, showing `N. O.` / `ARM` / `N. C.` and the bottom of `STORAGE/PR...` in one frame; PH2 crop x=2520 y=1150 w=470 h=130 at 4x for a second instance.

rulings.currentText: "Independently confirmed as a *pattern* on PH2: section 2 reads left 790/850, middle 975/1035, right 1155/1215, and the same x positions repeat in every band. [verified] - PH2"
